issue.title: sase-core flake: telemetry store concurrent_writers_preserve_every_delta fails under full-gate load
issue.description:
Proposed by epic phase sase-157.4 (sase-core macOS portability epic) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; filed by the sase-157 land agent. Not caused by sase-157 (the epic never touched telemetry).

Repo: sase-core. Test: `crates/sase_core/src/telemetry/store.rs` `tests::concurrent_writers_preserve_every_delta` (~line 2418).

Observation (sase-157.4 note, 2026-09-21): failed once during `./scripts/check.sh all` on Linux (3192 passed, 1 failed) under full-gate parallel load, then passed on a focused rerun of the same tree.

The test runs 10 rounds of 4 barrier-synchronized threads each calling `record_batch(..., Duration::from_secs(5))` against one sqlite file and then `query_instant(..., Duration::from_secs(1))`, with `.unwrap()` on both. The failure message was not captured, so it is unknown whether it was a lost delta (the assertion) or a busy-timeout error surfacing through an `unwrap()` when the host is saturated. First step: reproduce under load (e.g. run the sase_core suite with high parallelism or under `stress`) and capture the panic message before choosing a fix.

Now that the macOS CI leg in sase-core is required (sase-157.9), a flake here can also turn master red on either platform.

task_type_fields.evidence: 1 failure observed in one full-gate `./scripts/check.sh all` run on Linux under parallel load (3192 passed, 1 failed); passed on focused rerun on the unchanged tree. Serial reproduction not attempted; failure message not captured. Reported by sase-157.4.
